note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Kentucky's November 3, 2026 state and local ballot carries the Republican and Democratic parties, the Kentucky Party (two candidates), independents and declared write-ins; there is no statewide executive race. Kentucky parties do not endorse in contested primaries (the Franklin County Democratic Party's page says so), and most party pages list their nominees without calling it an endorsement. Only two pages call their lists endorsements: the Franklin County Democratic Party's '2026 Democratic Candidates' ('We're excited to endorse these Democratic Candidates') and the Kenton County Democratic Party's '2026 Candidates', which its own 2026 Voter Guide presents as 'the candidates endorsed by the Kenton County Democratic Party for the General Election'; both include nonpartisan city and school contests. Everything else is under 'other_support', with the page's own wording in 'kind', never to be shown as an endorsement: the Republican Party of Kentucky's 'Elected Officials & Candidates' (its 2026 legislative candidates; names, office and district only were read, never the campaign addresses the cards carry), the Jefferson, Campbell, McCracken, Hardin and Jessamine county Republican pages, and the Fayette, Boone, Daviess, Bourbon, Jessamine, Mercer, Nelson, Shelby, McCracken and Madison county Democratic pages. A line on a partisan contest adds nothing to the party printed on the ballot; lines on nonpartisan contests (Louisville Metro Council, Lexington's mayor and council, other city councils, school boards, judges) are the ones that say something the ballot does not. The Hardin County Republican Party's page lists every candidate in each nonpartisan contest and marks some '(R)': only the marked names are recorded. Bourbon County's post (January 30), Shelby County's home page and Jessamine County Democrats' page were written for the May primary; a candidate there who is not on the November list carries 'election' when the primary list is loaded, and is otherwise unmatched. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Leese for Leesa Unger, Herrmann for Herrman, Salwaechter for Saalwaechter, Corneilson for Cornelison, O'Neill for Oneill, McNamara for Mc Namara, Christopher for the ballot's Chistopher McVey). Lines whose district on the page differs from the November list are left unmatched rather than guessed (see the reasons). Federal offices on these pages are outside this file. Read on 2026-10-03 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record is kept only if the page still showed it (none was lost), and the Kenton voter guide's endorsement sentence and Franklin's were found again. Facebook pages are social media and were not read. Things for a person to look at: the Franklin County Democratic Party's page puts Erika Hancock in House District 56 and David Graves in 57, the reverse of the November list; Boone County Democrats put Lianna Nguyen in Commissioner District 3 (the list says 2); the Republican Party of Kentucky's page puts Carrie Sanders McKeehan in House District 41 (the list and the Jefferson County party say 38); and the Franklin County page lists Eric Whisman for magistrate District 6, a contest the November list as loaded does not have.
